mission_3.prediction: I compared the potential field settings on both the open and constrained maps. First, I increased the repulsion strength from 0.70 to 1.30, then increased the influence distance from 1.00 m to 1.50 m, keeping the step size at 0.08 m. On the open map, both settings produced complete paths with small adjustments near the person. On the constrained map, social_1 found a complete path, but social_2 got stuck oscillating near the wall and person. This shows that stronger repulsion does not always improve navigation, especially when there is limited space.
mission_3.comparison:
For A*, social_2 had the largest minimum person clearance at 0.812 m, compared to 0.733 m for the baseline. Personal-space time decreased from 1.5 seconds to 0 seconds. It also finished slightly faster, taking 46.44 seconds instead of 46.70 seconds, and traveled a little less distance (13.129 m compared to 13.192 m).
For RRT, social_1 had the largest clearance at 1.741 m, compared to 1.730 m for the baseline. Both had 0 seconds of personal-space exposure. Social_1 also finished slightly faster (43.41 seconds compared to 44.14 seconds) and traveled slightly less distance (11.522 m compared to 11.552 m).
All six trials succeeded. In these results, the wider spacing did not increase execution time or traveled distance, although the differences were small.
mission_3.recommendation:
I would keep A* with social_2 for this scenario. It succeeded with a minimum person clearance of 0.812 m, took 46.44 seconds, and traveled 13.129 m. Compared to the A* baseline, which had a clearance of 0.733 m and took 46.70 seconds, social_2 kept more distance from the person without increasing travel time or distance. It also reduced personal-space exposure from 1.5 seconds to 0 seconds.
However, these trials only tested stationary people. They cannot show how the robot would react if someone suddenly crossed its path, changed direction, or stopped unexpectedly. Testing with moving people would help us understand whether the robot can adjust its route safely in real time.
